name: BESTLIFE2030 grants for biodiversity in EU Overseas
summary: EU-funded grants, coordinated by IUCN, for locally led projects that conserve and restore biodiversity in the EU's outermost regions and Overseas Countries and Territories, run as regional calls for proposals.

geography.label: EU outermost regions (ORs) and Overseas Countries and Territories (OCTs)

pool.note: Across all four BESTLIFE2030 calls, including the ones already run

reporting: Projects track results against a logframe with SMART indicators and must contribute to at least one of the programme's mandatory biodiversity indicators.

steps: Full proposal with detailed budget, if invited

eligibility.rule: Legal entity registered in an OR or OCT; not an international organisation, individual consultant or sole trader
Directly responsible for preparing and running the project, not acting as an intermediary
Has a bank account in the organisation's name in the establishment or project location
Runs a project lasting 18 to 36 months, including potential extensions
Starts the project between July and September 2027
Is not a fundamentally research-based project
Is not in a situation listed in the European Commission's EDES system

documents: Signed co-applicant mandate, if applying with co-applicants
Co-applicant sworn statement, if applying with co-applicants

status.quote: The 3rd call for proposals is now open!

deadline.quote: Concept notes must be submitted by 8 December 2026 at 14:00 CET.

status.quote: With two calls now completed and two additional calls planned, BESTLIFE2030 is progressing steadily towards full implementation of its €23.4 million budget.

pool.quote: its overall €23.4 million budget, expected to support approximately 234 projects across four calls.

administered_by.quote: the IUCN EU Representative Office, as coordinator, working alongside the following organizations to execute the BESTLIFE2030 project

applicant_types.quote: Local non-profit organisations, local non-governmental organisations (NGOs); • Local civil society organisations (CSOs); • Local community-based organisations (CBOs); • SMEs as defined by the European Commission2; • Local research institutes and organisations (provided eligible activities are implemented); • Local sub-governmental bodies, e.g. municipalities and groups thereof;

geography.quote: is a granting mechanism focusing on preserving and restoring biodiversity in the EU's outermost regions (ORs) and Overseas Countries and Territories (OCTs)

access.quote: Applications are managed through the IUCN Grant Management System and may be submitted in English or French.

window.quote: expected to support approximately 234 projects across four calls.

amount.quote: BESTLIFE2030 grants amount to a maximum of EUR 100,000 per recipient.

co_finance_required.quote: A minimum of 5% co-funding of the total budget is required

consortium_required.quote: The lead applicant may act individually or with co-applicant(s).

reporting.quote: All projects MUST contribute to at least ONE indicator from the 'Biodiversity' category.

effort.quote: The application process begins with an eligibility stage, followed by a concept note for eligible applicants.
Concept notes must be submitted by 8 December 2026 at 14:00 CET.
Shortlisted applicants will then be invited to submit a full proposal.
Complete the Full Detailed Budget form for the full project implementation period.
Complete the Due Diligence form when it is made available and requested in the application process.

eligibility.quote: A private or public legal entity registered in ORs and/or OCTs (*). International organisations (inclusive of regional organisations with international membership), individual consultants and sole traders are not eligible to receive a grant (**).
Directly responsible for the preparation and implementation of the grant project. Applications submitted by a body acting as an intermediary for a third party are not eligible.
Have a bank account in the name of the organisation and in the place where the Grantee is established or where the project is carried out
Project duration must range between 18 to 36 months (including any potential extensions)
Projects must have a start date between July to September 2027.
Potential applicants may not participate in the call for proposals or be awarded grants if they are in any of the situations listed in the European Commission's EDES system.

co_finance.quote: A minimum of 5% co-funding of the total budget is required

documents.quote: Download and complete the concept note budget summary in the chosen language.
